UX/UI audit — October 2026

Typeaudit Projectmcp Updated2026-10-30 Findings30 Ownerdm ui ux accessibility
On this page

Verdict

The admin is usable for one technical user who already knows the system. It is not yet safe for a second user, and it is not safe for an agent working in the same workspace at the same time. Two defects block daily use of Knowledge, and a layer of state, identity and accessibility problems sits directly underneath them.

Nothing in this audit is a feature request. Every finding is a defect against a screen that already exists, and every one of them was reproduced on the running build.

Findings

The audit covered the four screens exercised every day: Tasks, Overview, Knowledge and Access. Findings are grouped by severity; the full list of 30 is attached to the task in YouTrack.

P0 — blocked

  • P0Clicking a document in Knowledge crashes the renderer to a white screen. The document id is read after the list unmounts, and the error boundary above the pane never sees it.
  • P0Search inside Knowledge crashes on a miss. An empty result set is treated as a failed fetch and thrown, instead of rendered as an empty state.

P1 — degrading

  • P1Error and empty states are the same component. A 404 and a search with no matches look identical, so the user cannot tell what to do next.
  • P1The realtime badge never leaves “Connecting…”. The socket opens, but the state machine has no connected transition.
  • P113 form fields have no programmatic label. Screen readers announce them all as “edit text”.
  • P1Six text styles fall under 4.5:1 contrast in the light theme, most of them muted metadata at 11px.

Accessibility measurements

Contrast was measured on the rendered light theme with the browser accessibility pane, one text style at a time. Body text clears 4.5:1 in both themes. Every failure is in secondary metadata: timestamps, counts and two of the muted labels on the board header.

Focus rings are present on primary controls and absent on the board column headers and the rail icons. The skip link exists in the markup but is clipped off-screen on every route except Tasks, where it is also the only route that keeps a visible focus ring after a tab.

Tasks vs YouTrack

The audit is tracked as five tasks rather than thirty. Two P0 items are filed against the Knowledge module. The accessibility layer is filed as a single task with a checklist, not as six separate tickets.

UI-13  document pane crash       DEV-7891
UI-22  search empty state        DEV-7892
F-29   shared status contract    DEV-7896

Mirroring YouTrack one-to-one was rejected. It doubles the reading load, and the two stores disagree within a day because neither owns the status field.

Proposals

Three changes remove most of the risk. A single state contract — loading, empty, error, ready — shared by every data view. One token set for colour and type, generated from the same source the server uses for status names. One page shell, so the rail, the top bar and the focus order stop drifting between routes.

None of the three is a redesign. The cheapest sequence is the state contract first, then the tokens, then the shell; everything else in this audit can ship on top of them without touching them again.
